outcome: Bertalan Bodor's July 2025 preprint 'Structures with not too fast unlabelled growth' proves Simon Thomas's conjecture (every countable homogeneous structure with finite relational language has finitely many first-order reducts up to interdefinability) for the class S of structures whose unlabelled orbit growth is bounded by 2^n/p(n) for every polynomial p — a genuine restriction/case of the general conjecture, not a resolution of it.
summary: The bullet is Wikipedia's phrasing of Simon Thomas's conjecture: does every countable homogeneous structure with a finite relational language have finitely many first-order reducts (up to interdefinability)? This remains open in general. Within the 26 Jan 2024 - present window, I found one genuine new result: Bertalan Bodor, 'Structures with not too fast unlabelled growth' (arXiv:2507.16985, submitted 22 Jul 2025, revised as v2 13 Jul 2026), which classifies the class S of countable structures whose unlabelled orbit-growth rate u_n is bounded by 2^n/p(n) for every polynomial p, in terms of automorphism groups, and as a corollary shows every structure in S is interdefinable with a finitely bounded homogeneous structure and has finitely many first-order reducts up to interdefinability -- 'thereby confirming Thomas' conjecture for the class S' (quoted from the abstract). This restricts the domain of the conjecture (a slow-growth subclass) rather than changing the question, so it is a case of the problem per SS3.1, classified as partial/confirmed. I separately re-verified two items the triage's why-note referenced: (1) Bodor's earlier paper 'Classification of omega-categorical monadically stable structures' (arXiv:2011.08793) also confirms Thomas's conjecture for the monadically-stable class, but its first preprint dates to November 2020 -- well before the frozen revision -- even though its Journal of Symbolic Logic publication appeared in 2024; per SS6.3 the preprint date governs, so this specific confirmation is open_stale territory and is not the event this record rests on (I did not find any indication its content or scope changed materially between 2020 and 2024 publication). (2) Bodirsky & Bodor, 'Structures preserved by primitive actions of S_omega' (arXiv:2501.03789, submitted 7 Jan 2025) uses first-order reducts of the Johnson graphs as a technical tool to prove a P/NP-complete CSP complexity dichotomy; it does not state or prove any new case of Thomas's reduct-finiteness conjecture itself, matching the triage's assessment -- this is a related-problem/tool use, not a case, and is excluded from status per SS3.1. I also independently found a GitHub repository ('vibemathing/problem-wikipedia-644eb5bce5410548') titled identically to this bullet's statement, appearing in generic search results; its content is not a mathematical source (it appears to be unrelated tooling/content bearing the same title string) and I disregarded it as the triage did, treating it as noise rather than a finding. No AI system of any kind (LLM, machine-learning method, or automated theorem prover) is mentioned in connection with any of these papers; this is standard human-authored model-theory/permutation-group-theory work using classical growth-rate and orbit-counting arguments.
competing_reading: One could argue Bodor's class-S result is a 'related problem' rather than a 'case', since it is stated as a corollary of a structural classification theorem whose primary purpose is orbit-growth classification rather than reduct-counting per se. However, the paper's own abstract explicitly frames the reduct-finiteness statement as 'confirming Thomas' conjecture for the class S', i.e. as a restriction of exactly the stated question to a subclass of structures, which is the textbook definition of a case under SS3.1, so I classified it as partial rather than open with no_change_found.
what_would_settle_it: A proof or disproof of Thomas's conjecture in full generality (all countable homogeneous structures with finite relational language), or a further paper extending the confirmed class beyond S (e.g. to all monadically NIP or all finitely bounded homogeneous structures), would move this record further. Access to Bodor's full PDF/TeX source (rather than the HTML rendering) to check the acknowledgements section in detail would let me state with full certainty whether any computational or AI tool was used anywhere in the derivation, though nothing in the abstract, introduction, or search results suggested one.

judgement.doubts: The pre-snapshot 2020 monadically stable result is a case, not a full resolution, so it does not make the record open_stale (the summary's phrase 'open_stale territory' is loose but did not affect the codes). The bullet's 'finitely presented' is Wikipedia's wording; the record reads it as Thomas's conjecture for homogeneous finite-relational structures, which is reasonable.
